meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'Vitya', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Вить, если тебе нужна работа, я могу помочь.
examples.trans: Vitya, if you need a job, I can help.

examples.text: Тамара, здравствуй, это Витя Баринов беспокоит.
examples.trans: Tamara, hello, this is Vitya Barinov calling.

examples.text: Привет, Витя, ты хочешь сделать ставку?
examples.trans: Hi, Vitya, do you want to place a bet?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: Внимание! = Attention!. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А ну-ка, дай посмотрю! Внимание, ребята!
examples.trans: Hold on, let me have a look! Attention, everyone!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'water' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Vanya, the water! There's water everywhere!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'yesterday' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.en: to turn off, switch off, shut down
meanings.note: + acc. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn off, switch off', paired with 'выключать'.

examples.trans: Slavik, turn off the television, please!
I turned off the light in the room.
Yes, Mama. I turned it off.

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative = to turn a blind eye to

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

meanings.note: Дай! = give (me)!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Общий туалет = a shared toilet. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('shared, common').

прибрать.gloss: to tidy up, to clean up

meanings.en: to tidy up, to clean up
meanings.note: Colloquial everyday verb. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'брать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to tidy up, to clean up', paired with 'прибирать'.

examples.trans: Forgive me, I will clean everything up myself!
We need to tidy up in the kitchen.

examples.text: Простите, я сейчас приберу. Я всё сам приберу!
examples.trans: Forgive me, I will clean up now. I will clean everything up myself!

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: От радости = for joy. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'joy, gladness' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он бы сейчас до потолка прыгал от радости.
examples.trans: He would be jumping to the ceiling for joy right now.

examples.text: Мы с радостью сообщаем вам новость. Ваш долг полностью аннулирован!
examples.trans: We gladly inform you of the news. Your debt is completely canceled!

meanings.note: подать на развод = to file for divorce

examples.trans: They went through a difficult divorce.

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with
meanings.note: мы сами разберёмся = we'll sort it out ourselves

В + prepositional. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sort out, to figure out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!
